seed: Objects of type `reflection` under action ACTION3 with touching neighbours [player,target,wall] show mixed outcomes: pixels,w,y x1, pixels,y x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: a field of the object itself, such as its tags, pixels, visibility or layer. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Two-axes mirror game: H band row ah + V column av of 3x3 wall blocks, pieces as block sets, targets, selection read from 0 hole centres.
A5 cycles H->V->pieces (sorted by min block); A1/A2 move H or piece in x by 3, A3/A4 move V or piece in y; axes bounded, pieces blocked by bounds/other pieces.
Reflections: visible gray across V (r,2av-c), invisible occluders across H and both; skip piece blocks; per-cell stack piece>vis>inv>target>wall, ring=top, centre=first solid else top fill.
Re-extract by colour: wall/player comps of own+0 cells ranked by bbox, reflection rank over vis+invisible cells, targets merged at bbox gap<=4.
Hypothesis about reflection fields under A3 was a red herring (outcome = re-render as V moves); stateless. Unconfirmed: A5 order beyond observed, merged-piece split.
